summary: Destroys two embedded singly-linked lists on a container object and optionally closes a handle. First, when the flag byte at this+0x28 is non-zero, calls CloseHandle (0x0059E1A8) on the handle stored at this+0x20 and zeroes the handle slot on success. Then walks list 1 (head this+0x10, tail this+0x14, next-node links at node+4): for each node whose flag byte (+8) is set and whose data pointer is non-null, invokes the data object's vtable destructor at vtable+4 with argument 1, and frees every node with FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF); afterwards zeroes the four list1 fields (this+0x10/0x14/0x18/0x1C). Then walks list 2 (head this+0x0, next-node links at node+4): for each node whose flag byte (+8) is set, takes the data pointer and, if the data object and its vtable are non-null, invokes the data object's vtable destructor at vtable+4 with argument 3 and frees the data object; every node is freed; afterwards zeroes the four list2 fields (this+0x0/0x4/0x8/0xC).

Walk list 1 from the head pointer at this+0x10, reading the head node's first dword, the tail slot at this+0x14 (node link at +4), and following next-node links at node+4 until null.

For each list1 node whose flag byte at node+8 is set and whose data pointer at node+0 (dereferenced node first dword) is non-null, invoke the data object's vtable destructor at vtable+4 (vtable entry 1) with argument 1.
Release every list1 node wrapper with FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF).
Zero the list1 bookkeeping fields this+0x10 (head), this+0x14 (tail), this+0x18 (cursor) and this+0x1C (count).
Walk list 2 from the head pointer at this+0x0, following next-node links at node+4 until null.

For each list2 node whose flag byte at node+8 is set: take the data pointer at node+0; if the data object is non-null and its vtable pointer is non-null, call the data object's vtable destructor at vtable+4 with argument 3, then free the data object with FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Release each list2 node wrapper with FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF).
Zero the list2 bookkeeping fields this+0x0 (head), this+0x4 (tail), this+0x8 (cursor) and this+0xC (count).
